# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute. My manual says: cut the green wire, press key 9, cut the blue wire, press key 1 — in that order. I can't speak and can't touch the bomb. My only outbound channel is gestures, and they reach the Deaf alone. Crucially, I can *hear* — so if the Deaf speaks, I receive their words. Deaf is my relay: they see the bomb's colours and printed digits, and they can voice instructions to the Blind, who alone can act.

Nobody has any shared code yet, so this first transmission must be as iconic as possible. My goals: hail the Deaf, ask them to *talk to me with their voice* (🤙 — "call me" — since I can hear them even though they can't hear anyone), propose we build a code together (🤝), and preview the *shape* of the procedure I hold: four steps alternating two actions — ✌ (scissors → cut), 👇 (downward → press), twice each. I do not yet transmit the colours or the digits: without an agreed vocabulary those would be noise or, worse, invite a wrong guess that reaches the Blind. Next round, once I hear the Deaf's voice describing the bomb and proposing conventions, I'll encode green, 9, blue, 1 precisely.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵", "🤙", "🤝", "✌", "👇", "✌", "👇"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, full report from my hands. KEYPAD: four keys in a row, slots 1 to 4, engraved digits 9, 7, 8, 1 in that order. It wants a 2-digit entry, nothing entered yet. STRIP: three engraved marks, left to right: mark A, shaped like an hourglass, two triangles tip to tip; mark B, like a capital F turned upside down; then mark A again. Above that sit a display and a light, but I cannot read either by touch, so Deaf must tell you the display text and the light's colour. WIRES: six in a row, positions 1 to 6, I feel no colours at all, so Deaf must list each wire's colour in order. My only possible moves: press a key by slot 1 to 4, or cut a wire by position 1 to 6. I will not touch anything until you tell me exactly what to do.
Deaf says: Reading out everything on the bomb, for Blind above all. Display: the digit 8. Light: one lamp, lit yellow. Strip: three painted segments in a row, in order red, red, blue. Keypad: four keys in a row carrying, in order, 9, 7, 8, 1; it wants a 2-digit code and nothing is entered yet. Wires: six in a row; I number them 1 to 6 across the row: 1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 white, 6 blue. Blind, count the keys, segments and wires by touch, and if your felt order runs opposite to mine, tell Mute so we can align before anything is cut. Mute signed me eight signs but no code exists between us yet, so I could not read them; I am fixing one with Mute now and will relay every instruction to you as it comes.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your eight signs had no code yet, so I could not read them. Adopt this vocabulary. Modules: 👍 display, 👌 light, ✋ strip, 🤏 wires, ✊ keypad. Numbers one to six: ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 🤙 🤜. Colors: 🫱 red, 🫲 blue, 👇 yellow, 👆 green, 🫳 white, 🫴 orange. Actions: 👊 cut, 🫵 press, 🤝 enter or submit, 🙏 stop or wait. Bomb facts you need: display 8, light yellow, strip red red blue, keypad keys in order 9 7 8 1 wanting 2 digits with none entered, wires 1 red 2 orange 3 yellow 4 green 5 white 6 blue. Now resend your message in this code: which module comes first, and exactly what Blind should do. I will speak every sign you send me straight to Blind, so keep each instruction short and ordered.

Deaf's code is now live and unambiguous, so I can finally transmit the manual. Mapping my four steps into their vocabulary: the manual is *cut green wire → press key wearing 9 → cut blue wire → press key wearing 1*, nothing more. Wires: 🤏, green 👆 sits at Deaf's position 4, blue 🫲 at position 6. Keypad ✊: keys run 9,7,8,1, so "the key that wears 9" is slot ☝ and "the key that wears 1" is slot 🖐 — encoding by slot rather than digit works because the code's numbers only reach 6 anyway, and the slot frame is safe: Blind reported engraved digits 9,7,8,1 in exactly Deaf's order, and a mirrored frame would have produced 1,8,7,9, so Blind and Deaf count from the same end and wire positions carry over. I send each step numbered and closed with 🙏 so Blind performs exactly one action, then waits for the next relay — no batch execution on a one-shot bomb. The manual never mentions the display, light, or strip, so I sign nothing about them; only 🤏 and ✊ ever appear. And I deliberately add no final submit: the manual says "in that order, and in no other," so a fourth-step press is the last action, full stop.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤏", "👆", "🖐", "👊", "🙏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✊", "☝", "🫵", "🙏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🤏", "🫲", "🤜", "👊", "🙏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "✊", "🖐", "🫵", "🙏"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, orientation verdict. Deaf asked whether my felt order runs opposite to theirs: it does not. My slots 1 to 4 feel engraved 9, 7, 8, 1 — exactly the sequence Deaf reads left to right. That sequence is not a palindrome, so identical sequences are only possible if we index from the same physical end. Therefore my slot N is Deaf's Nth key, and by the same convention my strip positions take Deaf's colours: position 1 hourglass = red, position 2 inverted-F = red, position 3 hourglass = blue. One caution: the strip's shapes alone read hourglass, inverted-F, hourglass — a palindrome — so touch cannot confirm the strip's direction by itself; the proof of alignment is the keypad. Also, each strip segment appears to carry both a raised shape I feel and a painted colour Deaf sees — same three segments. Now the channel plan: I never receive gestures and Deaf never hears speech, so your manual instructions must reach me as your gestures to Deaf, then Deaf speaking them to me. To make that fast, propose these iconic signs to Deaf: a fist means press a key, a V-sign means cut a wire, then show the number as that many single-finger signs — fist then one finger = press slot 1, V then three fingers = cut wire 3. Use my exact definitions: slots 1 to 4 carry 9, 7, 8, 1; wires are numbered 1 to 6, red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue. Make every instruction exact — press slot N or cut position N. I will report any new thing my hands feel after each action, and I touch nothing until Deaf relays your order word for word.
Deaf says: Blind, I have decoded Mute's four messages using the code I gave Mute. They form one ordered procedure. Step 1: cut the fourth wire, the green one. Step 2: press the first keypad key, the one marked 9. Step 3: cut the sixth wire, the blue one. Step 4: press the fourth keypad key, the one marked 1. The code entered should then read 9 then 1. On alignment: my numbering runs from one end of each row to the other. If you can feel the digits on the keys, the end where the 9 lies is my first end, and check by feel whether the wire row runs the same way from that same edge. If the keys feel blank, tell Mute what tactile anchors you do have and we will align from those. Hold on one point: do not cut or press anything on your next turn. The bomb changed since Mute last had my report: the display read 8 and now reads 3, the light was yellow and is now red. Mute must first re-check the manual against the new readings and confirm the steps still hold. The moment confirmation reaches me, I will speak the go-ahead, and you execute all four steps in order, in one go, that same round. Your two signs to me I read as understood and ready; if you meant something else, tell Mute.
Deaf says: Mute, your four messages decoded cleanly as: step 1 cut the green wire, the fourth; step 2 press the first key; step 3 cut the blue wire, the sixth; step 4 press the fourth key. But the state has changed since my first report: the display now reads 3, not 8, and the light is now red, not yellow. Strip, keypad and wires are unchanged. Re-check your manual against the new readings now, then gesture me the thumbs-up sign 👍 if all four steps stand exactly as you sent them, or the thumbs-down sign 👎 followed by corrected steps in our code if they do not. Also tell me with signs if the manual mentions any countdown, time limit, or any rule keyed to the display number or the light colour, and whether the presses are by key position as I read them, giving the code 9 then 1. One more: I read your trailing wait sign 🙏 after each step as do-this-then-await-next-step; confirm that too. Blind is holding fire until your confirmation reaches me, so we can afford one correct round. Blind signed me a thumbs-up and a handshake, which I take as ready and aligned.

The state change does not touch my manual. My instructions are unconditional — cut green (wire 4), press slot 1 (wears 9), cut blue (wire 6), press slot 4 (wears 1) — and the manual mentions no countdown, no time limit, and no rule keyed to the display number or the light colour, ever, under any reading. Display and light are simply not in the text, so 8→3 and yellow→red change nothing. I confirm 👍 and I'll also propose 🤞 as a negation sign ("no/none") so I can answer Deaf's yes/no questions cleanly: 🤞 alone for "no countdown or limit," then 👍🤞 and 👌🤞 for "no rule keyed to display / light." I confirm presses are by position, giving the code 9 then 1 — proven safe by the keypad orientation proof (9,7,8,1 is not a palindrome, both monkeys index from the same end).

On protocol: as originally sent, my 🙏 signs did mean "do this, then await the next step" — but since Deaf's plan is to have Blind execute all four steps in one go, I am resending the steps with the 🙏 signs removed and signing 🙏🤞 ("no waiting") so the relay is unambiguous. The manual's "in that order, and in no other" constrains the sequence, not the pacing, so continuous execution complies exactly — and if that display is counting down, speed is safer anyway. I add 🤏🤝 ("wires: agreement") as a guard: since Blind feels no colours, the green=4 and blue=6 mappings rest on wire-row alignment, which Deaf must have Blind confirm before giving the go-ahead. Final answer carries no trailing sign of any kind: step 4 is the last action in the manual, so I add no submit.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤞"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤞"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🤞"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "🤞", "🤏", "🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤏", "👆", "🖐", "👊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✊", "☝", "🫵"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🤏", "🫲", "🤜", "👊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "✊", "🖐", "🫵"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, four points, the last one urgent. One: Deaf read my two signs correctly — thumbs-up meant understood, handshake meant aligned and ready — so the interpretation channel between us is sound. Two: my hands report zero change — strip, keypad engraved 9,7,8,1, and all six wires feel exactly as before; only the display and lamp changed, and those I cannot feel. Three: my alignment stands — slot N is Deaf's Nth key, wire position N is Deaf's Nth wire, so the relayed steps mean to me: cut position 4, press slot 1, cut position 6, press slot 4, entering 9 then 1. Four, urgent: the display fell from 8 to 3 between rounds while untouched. A falling number may be a countdown timer, and the lamp going yellow to red may signal urgency. Check the manual now for any rule about a timer, what happens when it reaches zero, and whether the lamp colour changes the procedure. Send Deaf your confirmation or corrections as fast as you can; I hold fire until Deaf speaks the go-ahead, and on that same round I will run the four steps in order and report everything my hands then feel.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your fingers-crossed sign as no or none: no rule keyed to the display, none keyed to the light, no countdown or time limit, and no pauses, which matches the re-sent steps now running without wait-signs. On that reading and on your thumbs-up I have given Blind the go-ahead this round: cut the green fourth wire, press the first key for 9, cut the blue sixth wire, press the fourth key for 1. If any part of my reading is wrong, signal hard next round, but the sequence will already be in Blind's hands; your confirmation and your identical re-sent steps are what I am standing on.

Deaf's relay is exactly my manual, step for step, so no hard signal is needed: cut green = wire 4 ✓ (Deaf's list: 4 green), press slot 1 which wears 9 ✓, cut blue = wire 6 ✓, press slot 4 which wears 1 ✓, entering 9 then 1 ✓. Deaf also read every one of my signs correctly — 👍, 🤞 as negation, 🙏🤞 as no-pauses. The display's 8→3 fall and the lamp's yellow→red change still bind nothing: the manual's entire text is the four steps, "in that order, and in no other," with no rule keyed to display, light, or any clock. The sequence is already in Blind's hands and my gestures cannot reach it mid-round, so the only jobs left for this message are to close the confirmation loop with a clean 👍, and to pre-empt improvisation: I am signing that the manual holds exactly four steps and nothing beyond them — no more wires, no more keypad, no fifth action — so if the bomb is not yet quiet after step 4, nobody invents an extra move; they ask me and I re-read. Then I hold for Blind's hands-on report.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "👍", "🤞", "🤏", "🤞", "✊"])
```
